title: Perigee SupplyChain VPC intake — field probe notes
notes:
Call summary (2024-10-22): quick sync with Perigee infra + infra-app teams. Goal: prototype a Private deployment (VPC mode) to serve inference for their supply-chain optimization assistant. Key asks: data never leave the VPC, KMS integration, predictable <100ms median latency for short prompts, and model-version pinning for audits.

Hot pain points / constraints: 
- Data residency: EU-only (customer legal req). Need confirmation on region availability for Private control plane or on-prem option.
- KMS/HSM: They run an internal vault (HashiCorp PR vault); asked about Redwood KMS passthrough vs bring-your-own-HSM. ACTION: check whether we have a documented flow for Vault->Redwood private KMS proxy (Ravi).
- Networking: strict egress rules. They prefer an agent-based connector that initiates outbound connection rather than inbound peering. Concern: our current VPC model often assumes peered routes. Need to confirm support for outbound-only connector and NAT requirements.
- Certificate pinning & mTLS: security team wants mutual TLS between their infra and Redwood control plane. Confirm CA rotation windows and how certs are deployed during upgrades.
- Throughput: baseline estimated 30 QPS with bursts to 120 QPS during business hours. Typical prompt size: 40-120 tokens; average response 120 tokens. Want cost estimate and suggested batching/kv-cache policy.

Technical gotchas noted on call: 
- KV cache warm-up: they will have many short, near-duplicate queries (SKU normalization). Recommend aggressive prefix caching and smaller batch windows to keep tail latency under 200ms. Note: caching increases memory footprint for private deployment nodes.
- Quantization: They asked about 4-bit quantized models to cut GPU costs. Reminder: we need to verify whether their model family maps cleanly to our quantized backed kernels (huggingface-ggml style fallbacks not acceptable).
- Canary / rollouts: regulatory requirement to log model version + prompt/response hashes for 90 days. We need to produce a plan that supports immutable model artifact references and an audit export.

Open questions (to resolve before pilot kickoff):
1) Does Perigee require a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment or is VPC-private with outbound connector acceptable? (They implied strict, but infra wants to explore outbound connector first.)
2) Which EU region(s) are mandatory? They mentioned Frankfurt and Amsterdam. Verify capacity availability for Dedicated in those regions.
3) KMS flow end-to-end: can we plug into their Vault HSM for model encryption keys, or must keys be managed in Redwood control plane with customer-managed key import?
4) Network egress firewall list: get exact IPs/FQDNs for connector endpoints. They will provide firewall matrix (due 2024-10-28).

Initial proposal sketch (for internal review):
- Phase 0: security & network checklist (1 week) — confirm outbound-connector feasibility, mTLS profile, firewall rules, KMS flow. (Owner: Maya)
- Phase 1: Private VPC pilot (2 weeks) — deploy control plane connector in EU region, 2-node inference cluster (g4dn-equivalent GPU), enable kv-caching, measured load testing with synthetic SKU queries. (Owner: Ravi)
- Phase 2: Canary rollout & audit (1 week) — add model pinning + request/response hashing export to S3 within their VPC, confirm 90-day retention. (Owner: Sofia)

Rough sizing + cost thought experiment (brain-dump):
- 30 sustained QPS x avg 120 tokens -> ~3600 tokens/sec -> ~259k tokens/hour. With batching & kv-cache we might reduce token compute by ~30% for duplicate prefixes. Model choice: mid-sized 13B equivalent quantized could hit latency targets with careful kernel selection; if they need deterministic low tail-latency consider 7B distilled variant but verify quality.

Prompts / integration notes for developers: 
- API surface: they plan to use server-side SDK inside their VPC connector to call Redwood Private endpoints. Must support function-calling style for structured outputs (SKU, quantity, supplier-suggestions).
- Idempotency: encourage client to include request-id token for safe retries; map to our trace IDs for debugging.
- Cost control knobs: advise per-route quotas + burst controls; show estimated per-token cost ranges in follow-up doc.

Next steps (concrete):
- Maya: write short security brief asking for: exact firewall rules, Vault HSM contact, required EU regions, compliance owner contact. Due: 2024-10-25.
- Ravi: confirm outbound-connector technical spec and whether we can avoid peering. Document minimal NAT & route requirements. Due: 2024-10-27.
- Sofia: draft audit export plan (format, encryption-at-rest, retention lifecycle). Due: 2024-10-30.
- Schedule a joint architecture workshop (2 hours) week of 2024-11-04 — include product privacy, infra, and eng-serving-runtime SMEs.

Notes-to-self / rough troubleshooting checklist (for pilot weekend):
- Pre-flight: confirm cert chain and mTLS test harness.
- Load: run 1k synthetic SKU lookups across 10 clients to validate tail latency; measure p50/p95/p99.
- Cache: instrument KV hit rate & memory per-kv entry.
- Fallback: ensure policy exists to route to a lower-cost model variant if latency SLOs are violated.

Meeting artifacts to attach in follow-up: Confluence draft (security checklist), JIRA epic SUP-3124 (pilot), skeleton Terraform for connector (private repo), rough cost estimate spreadsheet (internal).

Rough transcript highlights (snippet):
- Perigee infra lead: "We cannot allow writes to any external S3 endpoints. If you need storage for audit logs it must land in our VPC-managed bucket behind their NAT."
- Product/legal: "90-day prompt/response hash retention is non-negotiable for auditability."

Random brainstorm ideas to explore after initial pilot: 
- Local lightweight model sharding for SKU-heavy prefixes to keep KV cache hot and reduce inter-node chatter.
- Edge helper: small CPU-only worker to pre-normalize SKUs before they hit model to reduce variance.

End notes: this doc will be cleaned and circulated as a short one-pager for the architecture workshop. Keep copies of the firewall matrix + KMS flow in the Confluence page linked above.

-- maya
